A memory system has two halves. The write path: during a session, the agent records what it learned — a preference you stated, a fact about the project — as files in the environment. The read path: at session start, the
loads those files, or an index of them, back into the context window. Many harnesses ship their own memory system — Claude Code's
is one — but you can also build one yourself: a directory of notes plus an instruction in
The same trade-offs as any always-loaded content apply. Memories accumulate, so most systems load a one-line index and leave the bodies behind
rather than inlining everything. And memories are
, so they drift: a fact recorded in March is loaded with equal confidence in June, after the project has moved on. A memory system needs pruning, the same way AGENTS.md does.
